items.title: The argument that “AI structurally centralizes power” because it’s currently com…
items.summaryText:
The argument that “AI structurally centralizes power” because it’s currently compute hungry ignores 125 years of super exponential growth in compute price-performance. 

Improvement in algorithms and continued hardware efficiency gains     means there is no reason to assume AGI-level capabilities will always require a data center to run.

Scaling laws are not laws of physics. They’re simply empirical relationships observed for particular architectures, objectives, datasets etc. Change any one of those factors and you get a different scaling curve. 

If the brain is any guide, true AGI will likely be very efficient. In fact, current scaling laws might a bug and not a feature. It shows how inefficiency of the ML algorithms we discovered so far.
items.summaryZh:
所谓“AI 在结构上集中权力”的说法，因为目前 AI 需要消耗大量算力，但这种说法忽视了算力性价比在过去125年里的超指数增长。

算法改进和硬件效率的持续提升意味着，没有理由认为 AGI 级能力永远都需要数据中心才能运行。

缩放定律不是物理定律。它们只是针对特定架构、目标、数据集等观察到的经验关系。改变其中任何一个因素，就会得到不同的缩放曲线。

如果大脑可以作为参照，真正的 AGI 很可能会非常高效。事实上，当前的缩放定律可能是一个缺陷，而不是一个特性。它说明了我们目前所发现的机器学习算法有多么低效。

items.title:
On tokens and prices per token.

I said I’d write more about this, so here goes:…
items.summaryText:
On tokens and prices per token.

I said I’d write more about this, so here goes: an OpenAI token != another model’s token. We compare AI prices in dollars per million tokens as if a token were a standardized unit, like a gram or a kilowatt-hour. It isn’t. Different models use and produce the exact same text using different numbers of tokens, which means a lower price per token does not necessarily mean a lower bill.

Imagine two identical pizzas. One is cut into 8 slices at $2 each. The other is cut into 16 slices at $1.25 each. The second place advertises cheaper slices, but the whole pizza costs $20 instead of $16. Bummer ... your stomach doesn't actually care about the number of slices you just ate.

I know you are hungry now, but back to tokens. In one small comparison spanning English, technical, multilingual, and numerical text, the tokenizer we use for GPT-5.6 Sol used 766 tokens versus an estimated 1,170 for Claude Opus 5. That's a very significant difference of about 34.5% fewer tokens. You can get the same exact text, but pay for all those extra tokens. The price per token doesn't really tell this story.

Even correcting for tokenizer differences misses the bigger point. What actually matters is price per successful outcome, and for that you can use benchmarks as a starting point, but really you have to try it and measure on your own use cases.

That's all. May the tokens flow.
items.summaryZh:
关于 token 和每个 token 的价格。

我说过会详细写这个，那么开始吧：OpenAI 的一个 token != 另一个模型的一个 token。我们以每百万 token 多少美元来比较 AI 价格，好像 token 是一种标准化单位，比如克或千瓦时。它不是。不同模型生成完全相同的文本会使用不同数量的 token，这意味着更低的每 token 价格并不一定意味着更低的账单。

想象两个完全相同的披萨。一个切成8块，每块2美元。另一个切成16块，每块1.25美元。第二家宣传单块更便宜，但整个披萨要20美元而不是16美元。真倒霉……你的胃其实并不关心你刚吃了多少块。

我知道你现在饿了，但我们回到 token 的话题。在一次涵盖英语、技术、多语言和数字文本的小型对比中，我们用于 GPT-5.6 Sol 的分词器使用了766个 token，而 Claude Opus 5 估计需要1,170个。这是非常显著的差异，大约少了34.5%的 token。你可以得到完全相同的文本，却要为那些额外的 token 付钱。每 token 的价格并不能真正说明这个问题。

即使校正分词器差异，也忽略了更重要的一点。真正重要的是每个成功结果的价格。对此，你可以用基准测试作为起点，但真的要在自己的用例中尝试和衡量。

就这些。愿 token 源源不断。

items.summaryText:
I think people don’t realize how much of the success of React is actually @shadcn.

I once referred to React as the actual “LEGO brick for adults.” But in reality it was more the description of the geometry of the bricks. The spec.

Shadcn is what people actually wanted from React. Reusable high quality components that also tunable. It’s a pseudo-library. There’s code but it’s actually meant to be digested into your context window and remixed.
items.summaryZh:
我觉得人们没有意识到，React 的成功在多大程度上其实要归功于 @shadcn。

我曾把 React 称为真正的“成年人乐高积木”。但实际上，它更像是积木几何形状的描述，也就是规格说明。

Shadcn 才是人们真正想从 React 中得到的东西。可复用、高质量、而且还可以调优的组件。它是一个伪库。里面有代码，但它实际上是要被消化到你的上下文窗口中，再重新混合使用。

items.title: Last week I’m sitting across a stealth portfolio founder working in a deeply uns…
items.summaryText:
Last week I’m sitting across a stealth portfolio founder working in a deeply unsexy space (at least from Bay Area standards)..

They’re lamenting about how how some of the critical contracts and partnerships that would give them credibility (and revenue and network effects) are basically stuck at the 1-yard line. This is a massively fragmented market. And this is btw just straight up pure bureaucracy. The champions, terms and everything is lined up. It’s purely a win win situation but summer and one random clause is the issue. And, it might cause them to not reach their ambitious timelines. 

And I’m sitting there smiling and eventually laughing and at some point they ask what’s funny. I tell them “do you know how long it’ll take anyone to do the same thing as you” - and this is with leverage and relationships that they already have. 

And, this in the short term is painful but in the long term becomes such a strong moat. That they’ll look back and laugh why they were worried about a few days when in the long term this is what will make them one of the biggest companies in the world. 

Unnecessary and 996 performative pain is not the moat. But building entrenched software and relationships that take a lot of pain is a moat :)

items.summaryZh:
上周，我坐在一位隐身模式的投资组合创始人对面，他在一个（至少按硅谷标准来看）非常不性感的领域打拼……

他们在抱怨，一些关键合同和合作关系——那些本会带给他们信誉（以及收入和网络效应）的合同——基本上卡在了一码线上。这是一个极度碎片化的市场。而且，顺便说一句，这纯粹就是官僚主义。支持者、条款和一切都已就绪。这纯粹是双赢的局面，但夏天和某个随机的条款成了问题。而且，这可能会导致他们无法实现雄心勃勃的时间表。

我坐在那里微笑着，最后笑了出来，他们问我有什么好笑的。我告诉他们：“你知道别人要做成和你一样的事情需要多久吗？”——何况这还是在他们已有的杠杆和人脉条件下。

而且，这件事短期内很痛苦，但长期来看会变成非常强大的护城河。他们会回头笑自己，为什么当初会担心那几天——从长远来看，这正是让他们成为世界上最大公司之一的原因。

无谓的、996式表演性痛苦不是护城河。但建立需要经历很多痛苦才能形成的稳固软件和人脉关系，才是护城河 :)
